## Al-A'raaf - The Elevated Places

(Revealed at Mecca)

206 Verses in 24 Sections

## Sections Of Surah Al-A'raaf

1. The object of the Revelation of the Qur'an.
2. Creation of Adam and the Defiance of the Devil.
3. Mankind warned against its enemy-Satan.
4. The guidance through Apostles and their rejection.
5. The Disbelievers shall not enter Paradise.
6. The Disappointment of the wicked in Hell.
7. God's only is the Creation and the Command.
8. The Ministry of Apostle Noah.
9. The Ministry of Apostle Hud.
10. The Ministries of Saleh and Lot.
11. The Ministry of Shu'aeb.
12. Warning against punishment.
13. The Ministry of Moses.
14. Pharaoh and his Magicians defeated.
15. Persecution of the Israelites.
16. The Delivery of the Israelites.
17. The Physical eyes can never sec God.
18. The Israelites started Calf Worship.
19. Mercy promised to those who accept Apostle Muhammad.
20. Muhammad the Prophet unto the whole mankind.
21. Punishment for transgressing the limits.
22. The Progeny of Adam will bear witness to itself.
23. The Resurrection.
24. The conclusive warnings against Polytheism.

## Important Topics

1. The people to whom the apostles were sent and the apostles, both questioned about the respective response to the apostolic ministries (Verse 6)
2. The measuring out of the deeds on the Day of Judgment (Verse 8)
3. The creation of Adam and the Angels asked to prostrate to Adam (Verse 11)
4. The arrogance of Satan (Verse 12)
5. Satan's vow to lie in wait and lead man astray (Verse 16)
6. The story of Adam and Eve's stay in the Garden and Satan's efforts to get them out of the state of bliss (Verses 16-22)
7. Piety compared to better garments for man (Verse 26)
8. People led astray by Satan think that they are guided aright (Verse 30)
9. For every nation is fixed a doom and when it comes, it is neither delated nor it goes before to. (Verse 34)
10. The forging of lies against God the greatest iniquity (Verse 37)
11. Groups of men and the jinn entering the Hell one cursing the other (Verse 38)
12. The entry of those who disbelieve in the signs of God more difficult than the passing of a camel through the eye of a needle (Verse 40)
13. Every soul burdened only to the extent of the individual ability (Verse 42)
14. The realisation of the inmates of the Paradise as well as the inmates of the Hell, and the discourse of the people on the heights, i.e., 'A'raaf' (Verse 44)
15. Those who take religion as an idle sport (Verse 51)
16. Those who neglect the Day of Requital (Verse 51)
17. The decision on the Day of Judgment will be final and the disbelievers would aspire for intercession and a return to the life on earth (Verse 53)
18. The creation of the universe (Verse 54)
19. Exhortation to man to call to the Lord, humbly and secretly .. (Verse 55)
20. Noah's deputation to the people to guide them to the right way (Verse 59)
21. The Deluge (Verse 64)
22. Hud's ministry to the people of 'Aad' (Verse 65)
23. Saleh the apostle to the 'Thamud' (Verse 73)
24. Lot's exhortation to the people and the fate of the people for not listening to the Apostle. (Verse 80)
25. Shu'aeb's ministry to the people of Midian (Verse 85)
26. Affliction to the peoples was to humble them down against the arrogance and the rebellious nature they had developed (Verse 94)
27. The hearts of the disbelievers arc sealed consequent to their own arrogance and revolt (Verses 100-102)
28. Moses and Aaron's mission to the people of Pharaoh (Verse 103)
29. The Miracles shown by Moses (Verse 108)
30. The encounter of Moses with the sorcerers of Pharaoh (Verses 109-120)
31. The fate of the people of Pharaoh (Verse 136)
32. The appointment of the Lord with Moses for the forty nights (Verse 142)
33. The insistence of the Israelites to see God manifestly, and the fate of the people at the manifestation of the Divine Light (Verse 143)
34. The worship of the Calf introduced by Samari (Verse 148)
35. The mercy of the Lord encompasses all things (Verse 156)
36. The prophecy of the advent of the Prophet Ummi, in the ancient scriptures (Verse 157)
37. The Holy Prophet Muhammad an apostle to mankind as a whole (Verse 158)
38. Water caused to gush out of the Rock by the stroke of Moses' Rod (Verse 160)
39. People turned into despised and hated apes for their arrogance and rebellious conduct (Verse 166)
40. The reward of the doers of good is never wasted (Verse 170)
41. Mountain made to hang over the heads of the people to make them realise the truth (Verse 171)
42. Adam's progeny in the backs of their parents bearing witness to the Absolute authority of God and the belief in the Day of Requital (Verse 172)
43. Men worse than cattle (Verse 179)
44. To call God with the beautiful Names of His (Verse 180)
45. None knows the Hour, the House of the Final Resurrection for the Final Judgment (Verse 187)
46. All men created of one and the same single self (Verse 189)
47. To seek refuge in God whenever Satan attempts to afflict with his misguidance (Verse 200)
48. The Holy Qur'an a clear proof and guidance from the Lord for people who believe (Verse 203)
49. To remember the Lord, aloud and silently, morning and the evening (Verse 205)
50. Those with God are not proud, they glorify Him and throw themselves down in prostration (Verse 206)

## Al-A'raaf Section 1 - The Object Of The Revelation Of The Qur'an

- Quran's revelation, its object
- Every soul shall be judged, and every apostle will also be questioned
- Deeds will be measured justly.

In the name of God, the Beneficent the Merciful

## Al-A'raaf Section 2 - Creation Of Adam And The Defiance Of The Devil

- Adam's creation
- Angels ordered to prostrate before Adam
- The Devil's defiance
- The Devil cast out
- Adam beguiled by the Devil
- Adam's seeking God's pardon

## Al-A'raaf Section 3 - Mankind Warned Against Its Enemy - Satan

- Mankind warned against Satan and his Tribe
- Sincerity in prayer
- Justice in dealings enjoined.

## Al-A'raaf Section 4 - The Guidance Through Apostles And Their Rejection

- The Apostles coming with the guidance
- The fate of the disbelievers
- The guilty ones shall accuse each other and shall themselves witness against themselves.

## Al-A'raaf Section 5 - The Disbelievers Shall Not Enter Paradise

- No soul is charged with any responsibility but to the limits of its ability
- The fate of the disbelievers and the reward the believers will receive.

## Al-A'raaf Section 6 - The Disappointment Of The Wicked In Hell

- The fate of the wicked and their disappointment in hell.

## Al-A'raaf Section 7 - God's Only Is The Creation And The Command

- Creation belongs only to God and God's alone is the Command
- The Resurrection of mankind.

## Al-A'raaf Section 8 - The Ministry Of Apostle Noah

- Noah's exhortation to his people to serve the Only God
- The people belied him and were drowned.

## Al-'Araf Section 9 - The Ministry Of Apostle Hud

- Apostle Hud exhorting his people to serve only God and none else
- The people challenging Hud against the threats of the wrath of God
- The punishment they suffered.

## Al-A'raaf Section 10 - The Ministries Of Saleh And Lot

- Saleh's exhortation to believe in and stick to Unity of God
- The people disbelieved and got punished
- Lot preached purity of life
- He was rejected, and the people were seized by a severe punishment.

## Al-A'raaf Section 11 - The Ministry Of Shu'aib

- Shu'aib exhorts his people to believe in and stick to the Unity of God
- His rejection and the punishment

## Al-A'raaf Section 12 - Warning Against Punishment

- Cause of the distress sent on the previous disbelieving people
- Warning with the Punishment

## Al-A'raaf Section 13 - The Ministry Of Moses

- The hearts of the previous disbelievers sealed against understanding as they were not faithful to the Covenant
- Moses' Mission to Pharaoh
- Signs demanded of Moses and his showing them

## Al-A'raaf Section 14 - Pharaoh And His Magicians Defeated

- Moses defeats Pharaoh and his Enchanters through the Miraculous Rod

## Al-A'raaf Section 15 - Persecution Of The Israelites

- The Israelites persecuted
- Moses preaches patience
- Promises delivery and the Heritage of the Hold of the Land

## Al-A'raaf Section 16 - The Delivery Of The Israelites

- The Israelites rescued
- They were still after idol gods
- Moses admonishes them to stick only to the True God who had rescued them and bestowed on them great favours

## Al-A'raaf Section 17 - The Physical Eyes Can Never See God

- Moses called on the Mountain
- None can by any means see God with his physical eyes
- Moses given the Torah

## Al-A'raaf Section 18 - The Israelites Started Calf Worship

- The Israelites making a calf and worshipping it
- Aaron faultless

## Al-A'raaf Section 19 - Mercy Promised To Those Who Accept The Apostle (Muhammad)

- Repentance and forgiveness accepted
- Mercy promised to those who followed the Apostle (Muhammad) and the Light sent down along with him

## Al-A'raaf Section 20 - The Holy Prophet Muhammad, The Apostle Unto The Whole Mankind

- Muhammad commanded by God to declare his ministry unto mankind as a whole
- The Israelites' rebellious behaviour
- The Miracle of water caused by Moses to gush out of a Rock

## Al-A'raaf Section 21 - Punishment For Transgressing The Limits

- Punishment for exceeding the limits of Sabbath
- The later generations
- The Covenant made with the Jews

## Al-A'raaf Section 22 - The Progeny Of Adam Will Bear Witness Against Itself

- The Progeny of Adam shall bear witness against each other
- Similitude of the disbelievers
- All beautiful names are God's

## Al-'Araaf Section 23 - The Resurrection

- God's plan is unbreakable
- The Time or The Day of Resurrection known only to God
- The Doom shall be sudden

## Al-'Araf Section 24 - The Conclusive Warnings Against Polytheism

- The helplessness of the false gods
- Prayer and humility enjoined
- To seek refuge in God against the Devil's incitement

translations.2: (The) Book (The Holy Qur'an.) (the Qur'an) hath been sent down unto thee so that there be no (Should not be.) straintendness or narrowness in thy (The Prophet addressed for the people.) breast about it, that thou mayest warn thereby (and it be) a reminder to the believers.
translations.3: (O' people!) Follow ye what hath been sent down unto you from your Lord, and follow ye not (any) other than Him (Any one, or anything else. This discredits 'Ijtihad' against any revelation.) , as (Your) guardians (or friends)', How little do ye mind.
translations.4: And how many a town have We destroyed, Our wrath came unto them by night or while they reposed themselves at noonday (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "7:159"]}>.) .
translations.5: So their cry, when Our wrath came unto them, was not but said they; "Verily we were unjust."
translations.6: Then certainly will We question those unto whom (Our apostles) were sent, and certainly will We also question the sent (i.e., The Apostles.) ones.
translations.7: Then certainly will We relate to them with knowledge for We were not absent.
translations.8: And the measuring (Of the deeds of every individual. Stands for the effectivity of the actions in the order of the Universe. (A.P.). Refer to Verses <{["Q", "18:105"]}>; <{["Q", "21:47"]}>.) (of the deeds) that day will be just; so whomsoever's weight be heavy those are they who shall be successful.
translations.9: And those whose measure (of the deeds) is light, those are they whose souls suffer loss for what they, with Our signs, did behave unjustly (Indicates that the actions will be weighed with the attitude of the mind towards the signs and not according to the quantity of the actions. The 6th Holy Imam Ja'far as-Sadiq says that even if a man stands the whole night in prayer and fasted the whole of his life, it will avail him of nothing if his deeds are not duly guided by the authority appointed by God. (A.P.).) .
translations.10: And indeed, We have made you inhabit in the earth, and have made We, the means of livelihood for you in it; little it is that ye give thanks.
translations.11: And indeed We did create (Start creating and fashioning - not a simultaneous action - but under a gradual process mentioned (A.P.).) you, then We did fashion you, then said We unto the angels; "Prostrate yourselves unto Adam;" so they all did prostrate themselves except Iblees; he was not of the prostrating ones (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "2:30"]}>; <{["Q", "2:34"]}>; <{["Q", "15:28"]}>; <{["Q", "38:73"]}>; <{["Q", "18:50"]}>; <{["Q", "40:67"]}>.) .
translations.12: Said He (God.) : "What preventeth thee that thou didst not prostrate when I did command thee?" said he (Iblees.) "I am better than him, me hast thou created of fire while thou didst create him (Adam.) (Adam) of clay (Refer to Verses: <{["Q", "28:76"]}>; <{["Q", "40:67"]}>; <{["Q", "55:15"]}>.) ."
translations.13: Said He (Means degradation in the state, Loss of rank rather than the change of place. (A.P.).) : Get thee down hence for it doth not befit thee to behave proudly therein. Get thee out; verily thou art of the despised ones.
translations.14: Said he: "Grant me respite until the day when they are raised up (resurrected)."
translations.15: He said: "Verily thou shalt be of the respited (This indicates that the life here is the life of conflict and not of compulsion but of free choice. (A.P.).) ones (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "38:80"]}>; <{["Q", "15:37"]}>.) ."
translations.16: Said he: "As Thou hast deprived me, surely will I lay wait for them (The issues of Adam.) in Thy straight (The Right Path.) (right) path."
translations.17: Then will I surely come upon them from before them, and from behind them and from their right side and from their left side; and Thou (God.) wilt not find most of them thankful.
translations.18: He said (God.) ; "Get thee out of this (state), despised, driven away; whosoever of them (The issues of Adam.) followeth thee, certainly will I fill the hell with you all."
translations.19: And O' Adam! Dwell thou and thy wife in the garden (State of enjoyment and bliss without any want or endeavour.) , so eat ye two from wherever ye two desire, but go (As already pointed out, this order to Adam was not imperative but explanatory to the requirement of the State in which Adam then was stationed (A.P.). Refer to Verse <{["Q", "2:35"]}>.) not ye two nigh into this tree for then ye two will be of the unjust (In relation to the state and not any disobedience to any definite order of God - In short Adam was informed that he will lose the state of comfort he was in, and not the final state he should be in. (A.P.).) .
translations.20: Then whispered Satan evil suggestions unto the two (Adam and Eve) that he might display unto them what hath been kept hidden from them of their shame, and said he (Satan.) : "Forbade not ye two, your Lord from this tree save lest ye two may become angels or lest ye two may become (Remain or live forever.) the immortals."
translations.21: And he (Satan.) swore unto them both: "Verily I am unto you a sincere adviser."
translations.22: Then he (Satan.) instigated them both by deceit (Aiming something and telling something else Refer to Verse <{["Q", "7:20"]}>. i.e. aiming at the first sentence of the Verse <{["Q", "7:20"]}> and telling the concluding words of Verse <{["Q", "7:20"]}>.) so when they (Adam and Eve.) tasted (of) the tree their shameful things got displayed unto them, and they both began covering themselves with the leaves of the Garden; and called out unto them their Lord (saying): "Did I not forbid ye two that tree, and (did I not) say unto you both that Satan is of ye both a declared enemy?"
translations.23: Said (Prayed Saying.) they (Adam and Eve.) "O' Our Lord! Unjust (In losing the state which was given - This is not the actual loss - The actual loss will be only if Thou forgive not. (A.P.).) have we been unto ourselves, and if Thou forgive us not and deal (not) with mercy unto us (then), We will certainly be of the losers."
translations.24: He (God.) said: "Get ye (Adam and Eve.) down (In State. This again establishes the present life as a state of conflict. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "7:17"]}>.) , some of you (being) the enemies of the others; and for you there is in the earth an abode and a provision (of sustenance) for a (fixed) time (Term.) ."
translations.25: (And) said He (God.) : "Therein ye shall live, and therein shall ye die, and from it ye shall be brought (Resurrected.) out."
translations.26: O' children of Adam! Indeed We have sent down unto you raiment to cover your shame and (for) adornment (Including all means of comfort.) and the raiment of piety, that is the best; this (Refers to the provision of the means of the physical and the spiritual development.) is of the signs of God that ye may be mindful (In using the said mean; healthily and harmoniously and constructively.) .
translations.27: O' children of Adam! Let (A warning to mankind against the mischievous aim of Satan in the field of the conflicts, though his activities might result in some physical progress for man. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "7:14"]}> - <{["Q", "7:17"]}>.) not Satan involve you into affliction as he got your parents out, from the garden (of the blissful life) stripping off their raiment, that he may expose unto them their shame; He watcheth you, he and (also) his tribe, from whence ye see (This proves the existence of beings invisible to man - Satan always attacks only from unexpected and unnoticed sources.) them not; Verily We have made the devils to be the guardians (The devil's activities will be affective only in those who have the affinity of the devilish characters.) of those who believe not.
translations.28: And when they act lewdness say they: "We found (This is a common excuse with all the wrong doers.) our fathers (acting) upon this, and God hath enjoined it on us," Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Verily God enjoineth not lewdness ('Fawahish' indecencies including nakedness - while circuiting round the 'Ka'ba'- as the pagans did while worshipping the idols- Other sins and crimes.) ; Do ye say against God what ye know not?"
translations.29: Say thou: "My Lord hath enjoined justice and set (Wherever ye be and stand for prayer-to turn to the 'Ka'ba' as the 'Qiblah'.) ye upright your faces at (each time and place) of prostration, and call (With full concentration and the presence of mind- Beseech.) upon Him, being sincere (With devout submission.) exclusively unto Him in religion; even as He brought (In accordance with the tendency with which life began, they will go back.) you forth (in the beginning) so unto Him shall ye also return."
translations.30: A party He hath guided aright, and (the other) party entitled themselves to error; (for) verily they took the devils for their guardians other than God, and think they, that they are the ones guided aright. (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "17:16"]}>, <{["Q", "36:7"]}>.)
translations.31: O' children of Adam! Be ye adorned at every time of prostration and eat ye and drink ye and commit ye not excesses; Verily He (God) loveth not the extravagants (This encourages the devotees to be well dressed and adorned as if they are going in festivity to meet the Lord. Condemns austerity, asceticism and luxury of extravagance in life.) .
translations.32: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Who hath prohibited (Rn. Or. the economical and the prohibitory problems in Islam. Every-thing on the earth is made for mankind provided it is acquired and used within the prescribed way and the limit.) the adornment (granted) of God, which He hath brought forth for His servants and the good things of the provisions?" Say: "These are for those who believe, in the (short) life of this world (to he) exclusively theirs on the Day of Judgment;" Thus do We explain in details the signs for a people who know (Who can understand.) .
translations.33: Say: "Verily did prohibit my Lord only shameful (Includes all kinds of indecencies.) deeds, those apparent of them and those concealed, and sin and rebellion without (any) right, and that ye associate (not) with God for which hath not been sent down any authority, and that ye say (This is a clear warning against the unwarranted conjectures of the modern irreligious ones, against the ordinances of the Qur'an and the Holy Prophet.) (not) against God what ye know not (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "7:3"]}>.) ."
translations.34: And for every people (Community.) is (an appointed) term, so when cometh their (appointed) term, they shall not remain (Tarry.) behind an hour (even for the least while) nor can they go before (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "63:11"]}>.) .
translations.35: O' children of Adam! When come unto you apostles from among you, relating unto you My signs, then whosoever guardeth himself against evil and amendeth (The criterion of piety and amending is to follow the revealed guidance and the divinely appointed guide be that an Apostle or an Imam.) (himself), then no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they be grieved (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "2:38"]}>.) .
translations.36: And those who belie our signs (the divinely appointed guides and their guidance.) and in pride turn away from them, these are the inmates of the (Hell) fire, and they shall abide therein.
translations.37: Who is then more unjust than he who orget (Accepting unauthorised opinions as the divine ones or actually belying the divine authorities like those of apostles or the Imams.) a lie against God or belieth His signs? Those (are they) unto whom shall reach their share (as decreed) in the Book; until come unto them Our messengers (The appearance of the angels may be to the individuals at the time of their death and at the first blow on the resurrection day or on any fatal occasion causing death for the individuals or collectively for the people as a whole.) , cause them to die, they (The angels.) (would) say: "Where is that which ye did call upon besides God?" They (The people.) would say "They have left us away in the lurch," and they shall bear witness against themselves that they had been infidels (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "25:21"]}> - <{["Q", "25:31"]}>.) .
translations.38: He will say: "Enter ye among the people who indeed have passed away before you, of jinn and men into the (Hell) fire; Every time a (new) (A fresh batch of the Sinners.) people entereth (it) it shall curse its sister (Fellows in faith- Companions.) (people); until they have all come together into it, the later of them shall say about the former of them; "O' Our Lord! These are they who led us astray, therefore give them a double chastisement of the fire;" He (God.) will say: "For everyone (of you) double, but ye know."
translations.39: And the former of them will say to the later of them "So (now) there is not for you any advantage over us, therefore taste ye the chastisement for what ye earned."
translations.40: Verily those who belie Our signs and in pride turn away from them, shall not open for them the gates of heaven nor shall they enter the Garden (of Paradise) until the camel passeth through the eye of the needle; thus do We recompense the guilty.
translations.41: For them shall be the bed of the (Hell) fire and from above them the covering (of it); Thus do We recompense the unjust (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "15:41"]}> - <{["Q", "15:53"]}>.) .
translations.42: And those who believe and do good deeds, task We not any soul but to its ability, they are the dwellers of the Garden of (Bliss); They, in it shall abide.
translations.43: And We will remove whatever rancour be in their breast, there shall flow beneath their abodes rivers, and they will say: "All praise be (only) to God who guided us to this and We would not have been guided had not God guided us; Indeed, did come the apostles of Our Lord with the truth;" and it shall be cried out unto them that: "(Behold!) This is the Garden of which ye are made heirs (Getting with a right of heritage.) for what ye did (This is in Contrast to the discourse in Verses <{["Q", "7:37"]}> & <{["Q", "7:38"]}>. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "59:10"]}>.) ."
translations.44: And will call out of the inmates of the Garden (of Paradise) unto the inmates of the (Hell) fire (saying); "Indeed we have found what promised us Our Lord to be true; have ye too found what promised your Lord, to be true?" They will say: "Yes." Then a crier (The first Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib (See Kashf al-Ghumma) of Mardwaih.) will cry out between them that "The curse of God is on the unjust (This is a very brief description of a 'Zaalim' i.e. unjust.) (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "57:12"]}>, <{["Q", "57:13"]}>.) ."
translations.45: Those who hinder (Misinterpreting the Holy Qur'an and the sayings of the Holy Prophet, thus hinder others from the right course of faith and its practice.) (People) from the path of God and seek to make it crooked (Misinterpreting the Holy Qur'an and the sayings of the Holy Prophet, thus hinder others from the right course of faith and its practice. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "18:1"]}>, <{["Q", "39:28"]}>.) , and they in the hereafter (Applicable to those who would do this will call them-selves as believers (Muslims) in this life.) disbelieve.
translations.46: And between the two shall be a veil (a curtain.) and on the heights (Overlooking both sides of the curtain.) shall be men who know all (Everyone.) by their marks, and they (Those on the heights.) shall call out to the inmates of the Garden (Paradise) "Peace be on you," They (Those addressed by those on the heights.) shall not have yet entered it, though they do hope (thereof).
translations.47: And when (they) (Those not yet entered the Garden.) will turn their eyes towards the inmates of the (Hell) fire, they shall say: "O' Our Lord! cause us not to be with the unjust people."
translations.48:
And will call the occupants of the heights (Ar. 'Araaf' A middle place between Hell and Paradise.) unto the inmates of the Hell who can recognise them by their marks; They will say: "Of (A clear warning to those who get puffed up because of their wealth and their worldly position. The first Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib says: 'What ye give birth is for dust. What ye amass is to go away. What ye build to be demolished. But what ye act is recorded and stored for the day of accounting or the Final judgment'.
 Though this is a description of the future-Quran gives us the past for the future, for the future to us is past for God, rather there is no past, present or a future for Him. Everything to Him or to whom He reveals is present. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "45:34"]}>.) no avail had been your amassing and what ye used to act proudly."
translations.49: (Behold ye!) "Are these they whom ye swear that God will bestow not His mercy on them? (whom God now sayeth) Enter ye into the Garden (Paradise)! No fear shall be on you nor shall ye grieve."
translations.50: And shall call the inmates of the (Hell) fire unto the inmates of the Garden (of bliss) saying: "Pour on us of the water or of what God hath provided you with; "They shall say: "Verily God hath forbidden both to the infidels."
translations.51: (Those) Who made their religion a past time and play and whom the life of the world hath deceived. So today We neglect (Ar. 'Nisyan' used in the case of God-means neglecting & not forgetting. This is a caution to all those who neglect the life hereafter and take religion lightly or even ridicule religiousness and scoff at the devout religionists.) them as they did neglect this day of theirs, and as they did deny Our signs.
translations.52: And indeed, We have brought unto them a Book (The Qur'an.) , which We have explained it with know-ledge a guidance (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "2:2"]}>, <{["Q", "2:23"]}>, <{["Q", "3:177"]}>, <{["Q", "10:37"]}>, <{["Q", "45:20"]}>.) and a mercy for people who believe.
translations.53: Do they wait (The Book is Complete so far as guidance and the blessing for the believers is concerned. Nothing has been left to be awaited except the final actuation. And when it comes, those who have neglected the Book before, will say this. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "35:37"]}>.) for anything but the final fulfilment (the resurrection)? On the day the final fulfilment cometh, those who neglected it before will say: "Indeed came the apostles of Our Lord with the truth; are there for us (now) any intercessors that they may intercede for us? Or could we be sent back so that we might act other than what we did act?" Indeed, they have lost (Put their souls in loss.) their souls, and what they forged hath gone away from them.
translations.54: Verily your Lord is God who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Arsh (throne) (Of Power, Knowledge and Authority.) . He throweth the veil of night over the day, which pursueth it incessantly, and the sun and the moon and the stars, made (absolutely) subservient to His command; Be it known! (that) His is the creation and the command; Blessed is God, the Lord of the worlds (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "10:3"]}>, <{["Q", "11:7"]}>, <{["Q", "25:59"]}>, <{["Q", "31:3"]}>, <{["Q", "40:8"]}>, <{["Q", "50:38"]}>.) .
translations.55: Call ye on your Lord, humbly and secretly; Verily loveth not God the transgressors (Those who remain aloof from supplication or disturb the peace and harmony of the others.) .
translations.56: And make ye not mischief in the earth after its reformation, and call ye on Him (God.) fearing (His wrath) and Hoping (for His mercy), verily the mercy ('Rahimiat'.) of God is well-nigh unto those who do good.
translations.57:
And He it is Who sendeth forth the (heralding) winds bearing good tidings before His mercy (The rain.) ; until they bring up laden clouds, We drive it to a land which is dead, then We send down water thereon, then bring forth with it of fruits of all kinds; Thus will we bring forth the dead (Example of the process which God's grace and blessings assume till the last stage of the fruit coming forth. The same process is applicable to all the dead coming to life. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:95"]}>.
 Persian: 'Baaran Ke dar Latafate Tab'ash Khilaf neest Dar Baagh lala rooyad-o-dar Shoora boom Khas (Sadi) The rain, the purity of which is doubtless, Raises flowers in a garden and in the saltish soil (rubbish or thorns). Refer to Verse <{["Q", "13:17"]}>.) that ye may be mindful.
translations.58: And the good land, springeth forth its vegetation (in abundance) at the will of its Lord; and that which is bad cometh not forth (from it), (herbage); but scantily Thus do we display (In Varieties.) Our signs to people who give thanks (React thankfully.) .
translations.59: Indeed, We did send Noah unto his people, so said he: "O' my people! Worship ye God (alone)', ye have no god other than Him; Verily I fear for you the chastisement of a dreadful day (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "11:25"]}>, <{["Q", "23:23"]}>.) ."
translations.60: Said the chiefs of his people, "Verily we do see thee in obvious error."
translations.61: Said he: "O' my people! No error is in me, but I am an apostle from the Lord of the worlds."
translations.62: I deliver unto you the messages from my Lord and advise unto you and know from God what ye know not.
translations.63: Or (Or is it that you wonder.) wonder ye that an admonition hath come unto you from your Lord through a man from among you, that he might warn you and that ye guard (yourselves against evil) and that mercy be done unto you?
translations.64: But they belied him, so We delivered him and those with him in the Ark (This denotes the reaction and the consequences to the reaction. Said the Holy Prophet: 'The likeness of my Ahl Al-Bayt is that of the Ark of Noah. He who got into it was saved and he who turned away from it, was drowned and lost'.) , and drowned those who belied Our signs; "Verily they were a blind (Blind at heart.) people (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "11:37"]}> - <{["Q", "11:48"]}> <{["Q", "23:27"]}> - <{["Q", "23:29"]}> <{["Q", "29:40"]}>, <{["Q", "37:76"]}>.) ."
translations.65: And unto (the people of) Ad (we did send) their brother Hud. He said: "O' my people Serve ye God (alone), ye have no god other than Him; What! will ye not then guard (yourselves against evil (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "11:60"]}>, <{["Q", "38:12"]}>, <{["Q", "53:50"]}>, <{["Q", "89:6"]}>, <{["Q", "46:21"]}>.) ?"
translations.66: Said the chiefs (The rich or the Leaders Refer to Verse <{["Q", "7:75"]}>, the mischief mongers.) of those who disbelieved among his people: "Verily we do see thee in folly; and verily we do think thee to be of the liars."
translations.67: Said he: "O' my people! There is no folly in me, but I am an apostle of the Lord of the worlds."
translations.68: I deliver unto you the messages of my Lord and I unto you, am a trusted adviser.
translations.69: Do ye wonder that an admonition hath come unto you from your Lord through a man from among you, that he might warn you? And remember ye when He made you successors after Noah's people, and increased you in stature (In strength.) , so remember ye the bounties of God that ye may be successful.
translations.70: Said they: "Come (Must thou come?) thou unto us that we may serve God alone and we give up what used our fathers to serve? Then bring that down unto us what thou doth threaten (Clearly indicate that the sign demanded by that adamant to the preaching of the apostles, was not the sign to prove the truth in the preachings but the destruction with which the Prophet bad warned and threatened them-The demand was only in mockery.) us with, if thou be of the truthful ones."
translations.71: Said he: "Indeed hath fallen upon you, from your Lord (His punishment and wrath); what! Dispute ye with me about the names which ye have named (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "12:40"]}>; <{["Q", "53:23"]}>.) them (your idols), ye and your fathers? For which hath not been sent any authority from God; Wait then, and verily I too, with you be of those who wait."
translations.72: So We delivered him and those with him by mercy from us, and We did cut away the roots (Destroyed even the last one of them stopping even their progeny.) of those who belied Our signs, and (they) were not believers.
translations.73: And unto (the people of) Thamud (We did send) their brother Saleh, He said: "O' my people! Worship ye God (alone) Ye have no god other than Him; Indeed came unto you a clear proof from your Lord; This is the She-camel (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "11:61"]}>, <{["Q", "91:11"]}> - <{["Q", "91:15"]}>. Even today there are people who, if not the 'She-Camel' the miracle wrought by Saleh, mock the other signs, the miracles by the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams of the Ahl Al-Bayt.) of God (which) unto you is a Sign, so leave it (free) to pasture in God's earth and touch her not with any harm, or ye shall be seized with a painful chastisement."
translations.74: And remember when He made you successors after the (people) 'Ad' and settled you in the earth, ye build mansions on its plain and hew the mountains into dwellings; So remember ye the bounties of God, and seek ye not evil in the earth, making mischief (Mischief invites perdition.) .
translations.75: Said the chiefs (The rich ones or the leaders, who had always been the mischief-mongers.) of those who were puffed up with pride among his people to those who were reckoned weak, to those who believed from among them; "Know ye that Saleh is sent by his Lord?" Said they (The weak or the poor.) : "Verily, in what he hath been sent with, we are believers."
translations.76: Said those who were puffed up with pride; "Verily we, in that which ye believe are disbelievers."
translations.77: They ham-strung the She-Camel and rebelled against the command of their Lord, and they said (A challenge from the people to prophet Saleh to bring down the chastisement they were threatened with.) : "O' Saleh! Bring us what thou didst threaten us with, if thou art of the apostles."
translations.78: Then seized them (unawares) the earthquake, so became they in their dwellings, motionless (dead) (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "51:44"]}>.) .
translations.79: Then he turned away from them and said: "O' my people! Indeed I did deliver unto you the message of my Lord, and did admonish you, but ye love not the admonishers."
translations.80: And (We did send) Lot, when said he to his people: "What! Commit ye a lewdness, which did not commit before you, anyone in the worlds (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "11:77"]}>, <{["Q", "15:61"]}> - <{["Q", "15:74"]}>, <{["Q", "21:71"]}> - <{["Q", "21:74"]}>, <{["Q", "38:13"]}>.) ?"
translations.81: Verily ye come to men in lust instead of women; nay, ye are a transgressor people.
translations.82: And (there) was not any answer of his people except that they said: "Turn ye them out of your town, verily they are a people who seek to purify (themselves)."
translations.83: So did We deliver him and his family, except his wife, she was of those who remained behind (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "26:171"]}>.) .
translations.84: And We rained down on them a shower (of stones); Behold (Consider.) ! then, what had been the end of the criminals (The last word of this Verse clearly titles the shameful act not as a sin but as a crime. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "29:40"]}>.) .
translations.85: And unto (the people of) Madyan (We did send) their brother Shu'aib; said he: "O' my people! worship ye God (alone), ye have no god other than Him; Indeed hath come unto you from your Lord a clear proof, so give ye full measure and weight, and diminish ye not to men their things, and make ye no mischief in the earth, after its reform; This is better for you, if ye be believers."
translations.86: And sit ye not in every path, threatening and hindering (Refer to note to verse <{["Q", "7:45"]}>.) from the path of God, him who believeth in Him, and seeking to make it crooked; And remember ye, when ye were few He multiplied you, and behold (Observe - Consider - ponder over – Remember - be mindful.) ye what had been the end of the mischief-makers.
translations.87: And if there be a party of you who believe in what I am sent with, and another party who believe not, then wait ye with patience until judgeth God between us; and He is the Best of the judges.
translations.88: Said the chief of those puffed with pride from among his people: "Certainly we will turn thee out O' Shu'aib, and those who believe with thee, from our town, or ye shall return into our faith" Said he: "What! Even though we be those who detest (The faith of the people i.e., polytheism.) (it)?"
translations.89: Indeed we shall have forged a lie against God if we return in your faith after when delivered us God from it; it fitteth us not that we return into it, save if it willeth (Willeth – Compulsion.) God our Lord; our Lord comprehendeth everything in His knowledge; on God (alone) do we rely; O' Our Lord! Decide (To give verdict on.) between us and between our people with truth, and Thou art the Best of Deciders." (Judges.)
translations.90: And said the chiefs of those who disbelieved from among his people: "(Beware!) If ye follow Shu'aib, certainly then ye shall surely be losers."
translations.91: Then seized them (unawares) the earthquake, so became they in their dwellings, motionless bodies (dead).
translations.92: Those who belied Shu'aib became as if they never dwelt therein; Those who belied Shu'aib (it is) they (who) were the losers.
translations.93: So turned he away from them and said he: "O' Ye people! Indeed I delivered unto you the messages of my Lord, and did admonish unto you; so how then shall I be sorry for a disbelieving people?"
translations.94: We sent not in a town an apostle, but seized We its people, with distress and adversity, that they might humble themselves.
translations.95: Then changed We, in the place of evil, good (Evil and good i.e., distress and ease.) , until they grew multiplied (To the extent that they were left to themselves – in the sense of having been given the respite.) and said they: "Indeed did touch (befall) our fathers (also) adversity and happiness; "We seized them suddenly (by surprise) while they were not aware."
translations.96: And if the people of the towns had believed and guarded (practiced piety.) (themselves against evil) We would have opened up for them blessings from the heavens and the earth, but they belied, so We seized them for what they did earn.
translations.97: What! Do the people of the towns then feel secure from coming unto them Our torment by night, while they are asleep?
translations.98: Or feel secure the people of the towns from coming unto them Our torment in the morning, while they are disporting?
translations.99: What! Do they then feel (Feeling secure against God's planning is considered in Islam as one of the major sins and the same is to feel despaired of the mercy of God.) secure against the plan of God? But feeleth not secure any one save the people (who are the) losers.
translations.100: Is it not (a lesson) guiding (enough) for those who inherit the earth after its former people that if We please We would afflict (too) for their sins, and set a seal on their hearts that they would not hearken?
translations.101: These towns - We relate unto thee (some) of their events (Stories.) , and (that) indeed did come unto them their apostles with clear evidences (miracles), but they would believe not in what they belied (Reference to the similarity of the attitude in the other people.) from before; Thus doth setteth God a seal on the hearts of the infidels.
translations.102: We found not in most of them any (faithfulness to the) covenant, and only found We most of them to be transgressors.
translations.103: Then raised (Sent.) We, after them Moses with Our signs unto Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they were aggressive with it, see (Consider.) then what was the end of the mischief-makers.
translations.104: And said Moses: "O' Pharaoh! Verily I am an apostle from the Lord of the worlds,"
translations.105: (It is) incumbent upon (me) that I say not anything about God save the truth; indeed I have brought unto you with clear signs (miracles) from your Lord, so send Thou (Pharaoh.) with me the children of Israel.
translations.106: He said: "If thou hast come with a sign, then bring it, if thou art of the truthful ones."
translations.107: So he (Moses) threw (down) his rod, and lo! It was a serpent clearly seen.
translations.108: Then drew he (Moses) forth his hand (out of his bosom) and lo! it was white (shining bright) to (all) beholders.
translations.109: Said the chiefs of the people of Pharaoh: "Verily this indeed is an enchanter (most) learned."
translations.110: He intendeth to turn you (Pharaoh addressing his chiefs.) out of your land; What is it then ye counsel?
translations.111: Said they: (The chiefs.) "Put him off and his brother, and send thou into the cities, collectors,"
translations.112: That they may (collect and) bring unto thee every enchanter (who is most) learned.
translations.113: And came the enchanters unto Pharaoh and said they: "Verily for us must be a reward if we be the triumphants."
translations.114: Said he: (Pharaoh.) "Yea! (even more) and Verily ye shall certainly be of those nearest (to me)."
translations.115: They (Pharaoh's enchanters.) (the enchanters) said: "O' Moses! Wilt thou cast (thy rod first) or shall We be the (first) casters."
translations.116: Said he: (Moses) "Cast ye (first)! So when they did cast they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them, and produced they a great enchantment."
translations.117: And revealed We unto Moses saying: "Cast thou thy rod!" then (When Moses did cast the Rod.) lo! it swallowed (one after another all), that they falsely demonstrated.
translations.118: So was established the truth and was made vain what (all) they were doing
translations.119: So (Pharaoh and his enchanters) were defeated on the spot, and returned humbled (Abased.) down.
translations.120: And the enchanters threw (themselves) down prostrating (in adoration)
translations.121: Said they: "We believe in the Lord of the worlds,"
translations.122: The Lord of Moses and Aaron.
translations.123: Said Pharaoh (Addressing the enchanters.) : "What? Believe ye in Him ere - I give permission unto you? Verily, this is a plot ye have plotted in the city, that ye may turn out of it its people, but soon ye shall know (the consequences)."
translations.124: Surely will I cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, then will I crucify you all together.
translations.125: Said they: "Verily unto Our Lord we return."
translations.126: And thou dost not wreak vengeance on us except because believed we in the signs of our Lord when they came unto us: O' Our Lord! pour (Grant us.) out upon us patience and cause us to die submitting (unto Thee, i.e., as Muslims).
translations.127: And said the chiefs of the people of Pharaoh: What! leavest thou Moses and his people to make mischief in the earth and to desert thee and thy gods? Said He: (Pharaoh.) "Soon will we slay their sons and suffer their women alive; Verily we, over them have hold (Ar. 'Qahir'- Here means Conqueror – Triumphant - One having supreme mastery or hold.) ."
translations.128: Moses said unto his people: "Seek ye help from God and be patient: Verily the earth is God's, granteth He as heritage (in Vicissitude.) unto whomsoever He pleaseth among His servants." And the end is (only) for those who guard against evil.
translations.129: Said they: "We have been persecuted before camest thou unto us and since thou hath come unto us;" Said he (Moses); "Maybe that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make ye the inheritors in the earth so that He may see how ye act (therein)."
translations.130: Indeed seized We the people of Pharaoh with (years long) droughts and diminution of fruits that they may be admonished. (to be mindful.)
translations.131: But when reached them any good said they "This is due to us;" and when any evil did smite them, they ascribed it to ill-luck due to Moses and those with him; Be it known! Verily their ill-luck (Man's own misbehaviour is explained in <{["Q", "4:78"]}>, but every one's misfortune is with God i.e., in His Knowledge.) is only with God; but most of them know not. (Ar. 'Ta'ir' - Lit., bird - here Omen, Augury. The people of Pharaoh used to draw Omens from the flight of the birds into a particular direction - As some in our days draw similar Omens from Cats and other animals, even men crossing the way.)
translations.132: And said they: "Whatever thou mayest bring unto us of any sign to enchant us with it, we will not believe in thee."
translations.133: So We sent upon them widespread calamities, (of wholesale death), and the locust and the lice, and the frogs and the blood, clear signs (miracles.) , yet they behaved proudly (arrogantly.) and so they were a guilty people.
translations.134: And whenever fell upon them the torment (The shocking and the shaking torment making them shiver.) said they: "O' Moses! pray unto thy Lord as He covenanted with thee, if thou removeth from us the torment, surely will we believe in thee, and surely will we send with thee the children of Israel."
translations.135: But whenever removed We the torment from them till a fixed term which they should reach, lo! they broke (their promise).
translations.136: So We did inflict retribution on them, and drowned them in the sea, because they belied Our signs and were heedless of them.
translations.137: And made We inheritors the people who were deemed weak (to inherit) the eastern (The Western and Eastern sides of the Holy Land is not that of the Red Sea.) parts of the earth and the western parts of it, which we had blessed therein (with fertility); and the good (The promise made to the Israelites.) word of thy Lord was fulfilled in the children of Israel for what they did endure; and destroyed We, what Pharaoh and his people had wrought, and what shade (Abodes - buildings high & low.) they did make.
translations.138: And We caused the children of Israel to cross (safely) the sea, then they came upon a people devoted (themselves) to the worship of the idols of their own; said they (the children of Israel): "O' Moses! Make thou for us a god as they have gods of their own. Said he, "Verily ye are a people behaving ignorantly."
translations.139: As to these people, surely in what (Idol worship.) they are, shall be destroyed (brought to naught.) , and vain it is what they do.
translations.140: (And) said he: "What! Other than (the true) God, shall I seek for you a god, while He hath exalted (Preferred.) you over (the people of the) worlds?"
translations.141: And (remember ye) when We rescued you, from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted (Subjected.) you with grievous torment, slaying your sons and leaving alive your women, and in this, for you was a great trial from your Lord.
translations.142: And We made appointment with Moses for thirty nights and completed it with ten (more), Thus was completed the term of his Lord forty nights, and (before he went up) said Moses unto his brother Aaron: "Take (Exactly so did the Holy Prophet leave 'Ali in his place - when he left Mecca on the Divinely Commanded Immigration to Madina and also when he left on the expedition to 'Tabuk'.) thou my place among my people, Act rightly and follow not the path of the mischief-makers"
translations.143: And when came Moses at Our appointment and spake unto him his Lord, said: he (Moses.) "O' My Lord! Show (Thyself) unto me, that I may look towards Thee;" He (God) said: (O' Moses!) never shalt thou see me, but look towards the mountain, if it remaineth firm in its place, then soon wilt thou see me, but when his Lord did manifest His glory unto the mountain ('Islam' i.e., Submission - applies to all creatures and not 'Iman' i.e., conviction, which is confined to the section of the intellectual beings. Therefore, this term, 'the First in Submission' refers to the 'Order of Creation' and the 'First of the Believers' refers to the 'Topmost' or the 'First' among the believers of the age in respect of this. Refer to verses <{["Q", "6:104"]}> & <{["Q", "41:53"]}> - <{["Q", "41:54"]}>.) , He made it crumble, and fell Moses down senseless: and when he recovered (his senses) said he: "Glory be to Thee (O' My Lord!) I turn unto Thee (repentant) I am the first of the believers." (That Thou canst by no means be seen.)
translations.144: He (God.) said: "O' Moses! Verily I have chosen thee above the people with My messages and with My words (discourse); take then what (The 'Torah'.) I give thee and be thou of the grateful ones."
translations.145: And wrote We for him, in the Tablets lessons of every kind and explanation of every thing; and (said unto Moses): "Hold (To stick firmly.) thou these with firmness and bid thy people to hold fast what is best (The Best of the Lessons thereof.) thereof; Soon will I show you the abode of the wicked."
translations.146: Soon will I (allow to) turn away from my signs those (who) unjustly pride (Consider themselves great without justification. With arrogance.) in the earth; while (even) if they see all the signs they will not believe in it; and (even) if they see the right way, they will not adopt it for a way; And if they see the way of error, they will adopt (Refers to the attitude of mind.) it for a way; this is because they belied Our signs and were heedless of them.
translations.147: And those who belie Our signs and the meeting of the hereafter, vain shall be their (good) deeds; shall they be recompensed save for what they have wrought?
translations.148: The people of Moses after him (in his absence) made of their ornaments, a calf, (Refer to verse <{["Q", "20:88"]}>.) a (mere) body which seemed to low; Could they see not, it neither speaketh to them, and nor it guideth them in the way? They adopted it (for worship) and they were unjust.
translations.149: And when they repented (Felt their failure against the argument.) and saw that they had gone astray, said they: "If Our Lord be not merciful unto us and forgive us (not), surely we shall be of the losers."
translations.150: And when returned Moses unto his people, wrathful and grieved, said he: "evil is it that ye have neglected (Thrown one behind, after I left you.) me; after me ye did make haste about the matter of your Lord?" and he threw down the tablets and seized his brother (Aaron) by the head, dragging him unto him; Said he (Aaron): "O' Son of my mother! verily the people did reckon me weak and had well-nigh slain me, so make not (my) enemies rejoice over me, and count thou not me among the unjust people."
translations.151: Said he (Moses) (praying) "O' My Lord! Forgive me and my Brother and admit us into Thy mercy, and Thou art the Most Merciful of the merciful ones."
translations.152: Verily those who adopted the calf (for a god) soon shall reach them a wrath from their Lord and an indignation in the life of (this) world; and thus do We recompense the forgers of lies.
translations.153: And those who do evil deeds, then repent (Condition for pardon is sincere repentance - with the determination to amend - not to repeat the sin thereafter.) they after that, while (in fact) believed Verily thy Lord after that is certainly Oft-Forgiving, Merciful.
translations.154: And when was appeased Moses' anger, he took up the Tablets and, in the writings therein was guidance and mercy for those who fear for the sake of their Lord.
translations.155: And chose Moses, of his people seventy men for Our appointment, then when seized them a shocking, prayed he: (Moses.) "O' My Lord! Hadst Thou pleased Thou hadst destroyed them and me (too) before; wouldst Thou destroy us for what have done the fools (May refer to the story of 'Samari' or those who wanted to see God manifestly.) among us? it is naught but Thy trial; Thou causeth whosoever Thou willest to stray and guideth whomsoever Thou pleaseth; Thou art our Guardian, so forgive us and bestow Thy mercy upon us, and Thou art the Best of the forgivers."
translations.156: And ordain Thou for us good in this world and in the hereafter; (for) Verily we turn unto Thee;" Said He (God.) "My chastisement, will I afflict with it, whomsoever I will (He Willeth not but for the wicked.) and My mercy ('Rahmaniyat'. Refer to note on Sura 1.) embraceth unto all things, therefore soon will I ordain it ('Rahimiyat'. Refer to note on Sura 1.) (particularly) for those who guard (against evil) and pay the poor-rate, and those who believe in Our signs.
translations.157: Those who follow the Apostle, Prophet the 'Ummi' (The Holy Prophet Muhammad. This word is used in the Holy Qur'an with reference to the apostles of God in general and the Holy Prophet in particular – meaning - that respect and reverence to be paid to them - and to this effect the Holy Qur'an has enjoined on the people not even to raise their voice above his and not to treat him as they do each other and warned his wives to be wise and careful than others in observing the teachings of Islam.) whom find they, written (in their own scriptures) with them, in the Law and the Evangel; commandeth he (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) unto them (what is) good and he preventeth them from evil, and maketh he lawful unto them the good things, and he prohibiteth unto them the bad (impure) ones, and he removeth from them their burden and the yokes which were upon them; so those who believe in him (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) , and honour (Refer to verse <{["Q", "5:12"]}>.) him, and help him, and follow the Light (The inseparable illuminating entities in all stages are the Qur'an and the Ahl Al-Bayt - (Compare - the 'Ḥadith al-Thaqalayn').) which hath been sent down with him, These are they who are the successful ones.
translations.158: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "O' ye people, Verily I am the apostle of God unto you all, of Him unto Whom belongeth the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; No god is there but He. He giveth life and causeth death, so believe ye in God and His Apostle, Prophet (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) , the 'Ummi' who believeth in God and His Words, (Both of Creation and the Legislature.) So ye follow him that ye may be guided aright."
translations.159: And of Moses' people is a party who guide (people) with the Truth and thereby do justice.
translations.160: And We divided them into twelve tribes (or) nations; and revealed We unto Moses, when asked him, his people for water: "Strike thou, with thy rod, the rock:" so gushed (As a miracle. Refer to verse <{["Q", "2:60"]}>.) forth out of it twelve springs; each tribe knew its drinking place; and We caused the clouds (Refer to verse <{["Q", "2:57"]}>. Similar instances have been authentically reported to have taken place in the case of the Holy Prophet Muhammad - once at the age of twelve when he had been to Syria along with Abu Talib and again at the age of Twenty-Five when he had been on business on behalf of Lady Khadija, a piece of cloud was seen travelling along with him just over him keeping him in shade.) to shadow over them, and We sent down unto them manna and quails; (saying) "Eat ye of the good things which We have provided you with"; And they (rebelled and) did no harm unto Us but they unto their own selves were doing injustice.
translations.161: And when it was said unto them; "Dwell ye in this town and eat ye thereof as ye wish", and say: "Put down from us our burden (of sins)''' and enter ye the gates making obeisance, We will forgive you, your faults; Soon will We give more to the doers of good to others."
translations.162: But changed those who did injustice among them a word other than that which was spoken unto them, so We did send upon them a pestilence from heaven for they had been doing injustice.
translations.163: And (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) ask them about the town which was beside the sea; when they did exceed (the limits) in the Sabbath when their fish did come unto them on the day of their Sabbath, appearing on the surface of the water; and on the day they observed not the Sabbath, they (the fish) did not come unto them; Thus did We try them for they were transgressing.
translations.164: And when a party of them said: "Why admonish ye a people whom God would destroy or whom He would chastise with a severe chastisement?" said they "To be free from blame before your Lord, perchance they may guard (themselves against evil)." (Become pious.)
translations.165: So when they did forget what they were warned with, We delivered those who forbade evil and seized those who were unjust with a dreadful chastisement because they were transgressing. (This Commands those who favour 'Amr bi 'l-Ma'ruf' and 'Nahy 'an il-Munkar'.)
translations.166: So when they proudly (Revoltingly. Refer to verses <{["Q", "2:65"]}>, <{["Q", "5:60"]}>.) defied what they had been forbidden, We said unto them; "Be ye apes despised, spurned (away from the human society)."
translations.167: And (recollect O' Our Apostle!) when declared thy Lord that He would surely send against them (The Jews.) until the day of resurrection those who would afflict them with a grievous torment; Verily thy Lord is certainly quick to requite (evil) and Verily He is the Oft-Forgiving and the Most Merciful.
translations.168: And We did cut (scattered) them in the earth into (different) peoples; of them (some) are righteous, and of them (some) are otherwise, and We did try them with good (The blessings) and (also with) evil (Misfortunes.) that they might return (to the Right path).
translations.169: Then succeeded after them (an evil) posterity who inherited the Book, taking the goods (Vanities.) of this low life saying: "It will be forgiven us;" And if come unto them the like goods they would seize it (too); Was not a covenant of the Book (of Law) taken from them that they would speak not about God save the truth, and (that) they have read what is in it; the abode of the hereafter is the best for those who guard (against evil); What! do ye not then understand?
translations.170: And those who hold fast by the Book (As the Holy Prophet left it with the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt.) and establish prayer; verily We waste not the recompense of those who amend (Also, the doers of good.) (themselves).
translations.171: And when We shook the Mountain over them as if it were a covering, and thought they that it was going to fall down upon them; (Said We) "Hold ye firmly what We give you and be mindful of what is (there) in it, that ye may guard (yourself against evil)."
translations.172: When brought forth thy Lord from the children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants and (when) made them bear witness upon their own selves (saying): "Am I not your Lord?" replied they "Yea! We do bear witness." (This We did) lest ye should say on the Day of Judgment "Verily we were of this (fact) unaware."
translations.173: Or lest ye should say: "Verily associated (Practiced polytheism.) (with God) only our fathers (Fathers & fore-fathers.) from before (us) and we are their descendants after them (following them): wilt Thou then destroy us for what the vain doers did?"
translations.174: And thus do We explain the signs in details and that ye might return (from the error).
translations.175: Relate unto them the news of him whom We gave Our signs, but he (See note to verse <{["Q", "7:175"]}>.) withdrew (himself) from them, so Satan followed (Joined.) him; so he was one of those who went astray.
translations.176: And had We willed, We would certainly have exalted him thereby (With the Signs.) , but he inclined (Clung to the material world - unmindful of refining the self-neglecting God and godliness -having no regard for religion or religiousness in life.) towards the earth and followed his vain inclinations, so his similitude is like the parable of a dog, if thou attacketh him he lolleth out his tongue, or leaveth him alone he lolleth out his tongue; such is the similitude of the people who belie Our signs, so relate (unto them) the stories, (This indicates that all Qur'anic stories have their application to human life.) that they may reflect.
translations.177: How evil is the similitude of the people who belie Our signs and unto their own selves they are unjust. (Doing wrong.)
translations.178: Whomsoever God doth guide He is the one who is guided aright, and whomsoever He suffereth to stray, these are they the losers.
translations.179: Indeed We have created (The justification for the allotment of Hell is the misuse or the neglect of the faculties and the consequent deterioration to the animal state.) for hell many of the jinn and the men; They have hearts (but) they understand not with it; and they have eyes (but) they see not with it; and they have ears (but) they hear not with it; they are like cattle, nay, more astray; These are they the heedless ones.
translations.180: And to God (alone) belong (all) the most beautiful names, so call on Him thereby, and leave alone those who use profanity (Vain use of or playing with.) in His names; soon shall they be recompensed for what they were doing.
translations.181: And of those whom We did create are a people (Refer to verse <{["Q", "7:159"]}>. A distinguished group - these can be no others save those whom God Himself purified.) who guide (others) with truth and themselves justly adhere to it.
translations.182: And those who belie Our signs, (One of the most prominent Signs of God is what is referred to in the previous verse <{["Q", "7:181"]}>.) soon shall We gradually draw them to ruin from whence they know not.
translations.183: And I grant them; (Those who belie the signs.) respite. Verily My scheme is (unfailingly) strong. (Effective.)
translations.184: What! reflect they not that their companion (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) (Our Apostle Muhammad) is not seized with madness, He is but only a plain Warner.
translations.185: Or look (Consider the instability of the transitory state and infer their terms coming nigh to the end.) they not into the kingdoms of the heavens and the earth and whatever things (God) created, and maybe that their term (End.) hath drawn nigh; then in what other words after this would they believe?
translations.186: Whomsoever God suffereth to stray (One who is not benefited or availed of the guidance of the Word of God.) there is no guide for him, and He leaveth them alone in their transgression, blindly wandering (bewildered).
translations.187: They ask thee about the Hour (of Resurrection) when will be its fixed time; Say: "The knowledge of it is only with my Lord (Refer to Mark 13/32. But that day and that hour knoweth no man no, not the angels, which are in heaven, neither the Son but the Father. N. T. Math 13/32. But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven but my Father only. Math. 24/36.) , None shall manifest it at its time (Time here is only a figurative expression for there is no other term for the conditions of the timeless realm.) but He; Heavy (The stage is so difficult to be grasped as it is within the limitations of the heavens and the earth.) shall it be in the heavens and the earth; it will not come to you but of a sudden." (It will be a sudden change from the dimensional state to the undimensional state not requiring any time.) They ask thee as if thou wert solicitous about it. Say: "Its knowledge is only with God, but most people know not."
translations.188: Say: 'neither I (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) own for myself any benefit nor harm except what willeth God; and had I known the unseen (Refer to note on verse <{["Q", "6:50"]}>.) indeed I would have had much of good and evil had touched me not, and I am not but a Warner and the bearer of good news for a people who believe?
translations.189: He it is who created you from a single self (Being.) and from it did He make his mate that he may dwell resting unto her, when he covereth her, she beareth a light burden and carrieth it, when it groweth more heavy they both pray to their Lord; ''If Thou givest us a good child, certainly we shall be of the grateful ones.
translations.190: But when He giveth them a good child they ascribe unto Him partners in what He hath given them; but most exalted is God above what they associate (with Him).
translations.191: What! Do they associate (with Him) that which createth not anything, and while they are themselves the created (ones)?
translations.192: And they cannot help them, nor themselves can they help.
translations.193: If ye invite them unto guidance they will not follow you; it is the same to you if ye invite them or ye be quiet.
translations.194: Verily, those whom ye call upon other than God are subservient (to God) like unto your own selves, so call ye on them, then let them answer (Grant your prayers.) if ye be truthful.
translations.195: What! are there for them feet which they walk with, Or for them are hands which they hold with, Or for them are eyes which they see with, or for them are ears which they hear with? Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Call (The reference may seem to be to the idols but with profound reflections proves that it is applicable to the living entities other than God.) ye all your associates and then scheme ye (your worst) against me (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) and give me no respite."
translations.196: Verily my Protector is God Who sent down the Book (Qur'an) and He guardeth the virtuous ones.
translations.197: And those whom ye call upon other than Him are not able to help you, nor can they help themselves.
translations.198: And if ye invite them unto guidance, they hear not; and thou seest them looking towards thee, while they see not.
translations.199: Adopt thou moderation (In all respects.) , and enjoin (To do good.) virtue and turn (Give up arguing with them.) thou away from the ignorant (Those adamant in disbelief.) ones.
translations.200: And if an incitement from the Satan inciteth thee (The Prophet addressed for the people.) , then seek thou refuge in God; Verily He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
translations.201: Verily those who guard (themselves against evil) when an evil thought from the Satan (Including Impious one - the evil doers.) afflicteth them, they become mindful (of God and get awakened) then lo! they see (aright).
translations.202: And their brethren (Of Satan - i.e. the impious ones.) drag them deeper into the error, so they cease not their efforts.
translations.203: And when thou bringest not unto them a sign say they: "Why not thou forge it?" Say: "Verily I only follow what is revealed unto me from my Lord; these are clear proofs (An eye opener.) from your Lord, and a guidance, and a mercy for a people who believe."
translations.204: And when the Qur'an is recited; then ye listen to it and be attentive, that mercy be done unto you.
translations.205: And remember thy Lord within thy self in humility and awe, and not (Less aloud.) aloud a voice, in the morning and the evening; and be thou not of the negligent (The Prophet addressed for the people.) ones.
translations.206:
Verily those who are with (In direct Communion 'Sajdah', prostration. According to the Ahl Al-Bayt – 'Sajdah' i.e., prostration at the recital of certain Verses is 'Wajib' Compulsory - in four Chapters of the Qur'an:
 Surah As-Sajdah (<{["Q", "32:15"]}>)
 Surah Fussilat (<{["Q", "41:37"]}>)
 Surah An-Najm (<{["Q", "53:62"]}>)
 Surah Al-Alaq (<{["Q", "96:19"]}>) In rest of the chapters 'Sunnat' Optional. Refer to verses <{["Q", "13:15"]}>, <{["Q", "22:77"]}>, <{["Q", "32:15"]}>.) thy Lord, pride not to worship Him; they glorify Him and (in worship) unto Him they prostrate.

exegesis.1:
Alif, Lam, Meem, Saad - (A, I., M, S).

The first three letters are the same which appeared in the beginning of the Second Chapter.

The fourth letter, Saad, is supposed by the commentators to stand for '_Sadiq'_- the truthful. According to (M.F.A.)- '_An Allah ul-Muqtadir us-Sadiq'_, i.e., I am God the Omnipotent True One.

The truth about the symbolic letters with which certain chapters of the Holy Qur'an start, which are divinely sealed secrets confided only with the Holy Prophet and his Divinely commissioned Deputies the Holy Imams. All the various explanations given by the various commentators are only conjectures<{["F", 1]}>. However, when God Himself destined it to be a secret, there is no use or there can be no point in any one unnecessarily endeavouring to manifest His genius in perplexing the public mind with any conjectures.

Once when one of the Omayyids came to the Sixth Holy Imam, Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq and in a taunt asked him, saying, _what is the meaning of the letters 'Alif Lam, Meem, Saad' and_ '_what benefit mankind can dram out of its use_? The Holy Imam replying to the taunt said:

_"Woe unto thee O' Man. What dost thou know of the secrets of God. The least of the meanings of those symbolic letters is this-According to the numerical value given to each letter of the alphabet:_

The value of Alif - 1

The value of Lam - 30

The value of Meem - 40

The value of Saad - 90

Total - 161

"_Go thou-this is a heavenly sign to shore that the rule of the land by thy brethren the Bant Omiyya shall last only for 161 years_." This prophecy derived by the Holy Imam from the symbol letters of this Sura came to be true, as the rule of the Ommayyids came to an end exactly at the end of 161 A.H.

Some think that the letters stand for the name of the Holy Qur'an. The Holy Qur'an is called '_Zikar'_<{["F", 2]}>.
exegesis.4: A living instance to prove the truth in this statement are the findings of the recent excavations in the various parts of the world where even flourishing cities have been found to be buried under hundreds of feet of earth covering them, from ages unknown to human history on earth.
exegesis.6: The people concerned in this Verse are those to whom apostles were sent. They will be questioned as to how they treated the apostles from God-and their messages.
exegesis.7: To know how the conduct of the people will be related to them refer to <{["Q", "36:65"]}>. The mouths of the people will be sealed, and the various organs of their body will be caused to relate what all they did.
exegesis.8:
'_Wazan'_, literally meaning weight or weightage, means justice-or the means of knowing or valuing the correct weightage or measure or worth of a thing. Weighing by God means that every matter will be dealt with, with perfect justice.

It was asked of the Seventh Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq whether the deeds of the people will be weighed on the Day of Judgment. He replied, "_deeds are not material things to be measured through any balance. Besides the necessity- to weigh, falls only to those who lack in the knowledge of anything. What is the thing or event which is hidden from God_." It was asked, '_what then do the words of this Verse mean_?' He said: '_Those whose good deeds will be more than their evils_'.
exegesis.9: The meaning of this Verse is made clear by the previous Verse, i.e., those whose evils will be more than their virtues, '_Yazlimoon'_ meaning here '_Yakfuroon'_ and also behaving with '_Zulm'_, i.e., with aggression. By '_Yazlimoon'_ also may mean those who had dealt with the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams, with '_Zulm'_, i.e., those who teased the Holy ones and martyred them, persecuted and killed their issues and their devotees.
exegesis.10: _Ma-ayish_ means the means for the fulfilment of life. In addition to all the material things necessary to sustain life, it also refers to all those powers and faculties which help man to rise to a higher plane to prepare for his spiritual destiny, on account of which the angels were asked to prostrate themselves before Adam. Iblis refused to be of those who bowed down, because he arrogantly despised the angels who bowed down as well as man to whom they bowed down. Arrogance, envy and rebellion were his crimes.
exegesis.11:
As said above under Verse 10, the spiritual destiny of man put him above the angels and jinn, so the refusal of Shaytan (Iblis) to accept man's superiority was unreasonable. It was egotism which prompted him to impertinent rebellion.

Allah created man with His own hands from clay and gave him His own spirit _(ruh))._ The essential quality of clay is softness which makes it adaptable to any form or shape-obedience and submission, and total submission to Allah's will is Islam-the spiritual destiny of man. So Shaytan, a product of fire, not having the qualities of adaptability, nor blessed with the holy spirit, was the first creature of Allah who resorted to conjecture, therefore was thrown out, eternally accursed. On his request Allah gave him respite (by saying): Be you among those who have respite. It implies that there are others, like him, under respite.

Shaytan has a large army of wicked seducers, and those who are their associates, helpers and deputies. The assault of Shaytan's evil is from all sides, and as said in verse 17; most men are led astray by him, while verse 18 says that Allah will fill hell with all of them.

For verses 19 to 25 see commentary of al Baqarah, <{["Q", "2:21"]}> to <{["Q", "2:38"]}>.
exegesis.18:
The story of the fall of Satan has been differently given in the Bible: Isaiah 14/12-20. For the details of the creation of Adam and Iblis declining to prostrate before Adam, and the fall of Satan, refer to Verses <{["Q", "2:30"]}> - <{["Q", "2:34"]}>.

_Iblis_ argued saying that he was created of fire and Adam of dust, and it will not be justifiable for a superior being to adore an inferior one, but Satan failed to consider the three factors in favour of the creation of Adam. He (Satan) was created of the evolution of fire, but Adam was by God Himself. Whereas God had said that '_I made him by my hands of my own spirit_'.

Secondly, Fire is unreliable for anything deposited with it is destroyed but earth or dust keeps in it anything duly endowed in it, and thirdly, Fire is proud and arrogant, and earth or dust is humble and obedient and accepts being moulded into any shape or form, whereas Fire does not. The first one who started conjecturing was _Iblis_. Conjectures about God are a satanic conduct, hence forbidden.
exegesis.19: For the story of Adam and Eve being placed in the Garden and their being beguiled by Satan and eating of the forbidden tree, See <{["Q", "2:35"]}>.
exegesis.30:
A part of them owing to their getting astray has earned perdition.

This Verse clearly says that the friends of the devils thought themselves to be guided aright. Hence the mere imagination of any people without the truth in it, to be on the right, is also a satanic delusion.
exegesis.31:
'_Zeenat'_ or embellishment refers to the cleanliness and decency of apparel specially against the pagan practice of going naked round the Ka'ba but the order is not restricted against any particular practice, but it has a wider significance. The second Holy Imam Hasan Ibn Ali al-Mujtaba used to put on very decent dress whenever he went to pray. When asked the reason of the special embellishment, he used to recite this Verse, and said, '_God is All-Beauty and loves beauty,_ '_Zeenat'_.

The real meaning of '_Zeenat'_ or embellishment is that which gives grace in the eyes of others, and it can be the external embellishment in physical appearance as well as the internal embellishment of high morals and the purity of the spiritual aspect of the individual. It is said that with the scholars, '_Zeenat'_ stands for cleanliness and decency in dress and their physical appearance and with the divines it stands for a perfect attention toward God. (M.S.)
exegesis.32:
'_Zeenatullah'_, i.e., the embellishment of God-meaning the embellishment made lawful by God for men.

And the external embellishment and the seeming enjoyments in this life, is there for both the believers in God and the disbelievers as well, but in the life hereafter, i.e., after death, the real embellishment and enjoyment and bliss, shall be exclusively for those who have earned it by the correctness of their belief and their goodness in action in this life.
exegesis.36: '_Wa 'stakbaru'_ declaring proudly against the signs, indicates the behaviour of the people with the Holy Prophet and the Holy Imams who are the greatest and the direct signs of God. The punishment which the people who misbehaved and annoyed the holy ones, is also mentioned as their being in the Hell for ever.
exegesis.40:
The example of the passing of a camel through the eye of the needle stands for the impossibility of the action. A similar example is given in the Bible. Math. 19/24.

"_And again, I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God_."

Mark the Biblical declaration-the doors of heaven closed to the rich-irrespective of their being good or bad, but Islam declares the closure against a vice be that in the rich or poor. According to Islam the entry to heaven does not depend on any economic condition but on the personal merit or demerit of virtue and vice<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.43:
One of the greatest or the highly intellectual pleasures of the life hereafter is the inter communion of the souls of the believers in the purest feelings of real brotherhood. Having the social pleasure of life in the hereafter in view of the Holy Prophet's saying regarding marriage:

"_Wed ye and meet ye and multiply yourselves for I shall pride over the greatness of the number be that even an abortion."_

The multiplication of the believers in God is undoubtedly desirable provided they are educated in complete accordance with the prescribed line of faith, i.e., the knowledge. The Holy Prophet said:

"_The seeking of knowledge is incumbent on every believer male and female alike_." (A.P.)
exegesis.44: '_A crier will cry'_-According to Ibn Mardwaih - a prominent Sunni Scholar (vide his Kashf al-Ghumma) the crier will be the first Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib. (M.F.A.)
